title: Waste segregation and environmental handover
audience: Supervisors, coordinators and trained cleaners who may be asked to triage, refer or document mould-related work in homes, rentals and commercial buildings, under an approved plan. Not a qualification or authority to remediate, demolish, or certify any building or room.
learningOutcomes: Identify the waste stream of each load in a described scene.
Record each load, its stream, its destination and its handover.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers segregating and recording mould-related waste. It does not authorise the transport or disposal of hazardous waste, and local waste rules govern each destination.

instruction.heading: What the guideline says about mouldy material
instruction.body: The WA Department of Health guideline says that mould is not considered a hazardous waste, and that bagged mouldy material can go in normal waste. It also says porous items that cannot be adequately cleaned should be removed or discarded. Those statements are WA guidance about mould itself. They do not settle the stream for material that is also contaminated with water from a flood or sewage, asbestos, lead, chemicals or other hazards. Those loads follow the stream set by the competent person.

instruction.heading: Plan before handling
instruction.body: Plan the containment of suspect waste before it is handled, and verify the local disposal, transport and contractor authorisations first. A contractor who proposes putting demolition debris into ordinary office waste bins is proposing something that must be refused. Keep the streams separate, record each bag or load, and hand over only by an authorised route.

procedure: Identify the stream of each load: ordinary mouldy material, contaminated water material, suspected asbestos, or other regulated material.
Confirm the authorised destination and transporter before handling any waste.
Bag and label ordinary mouldy material as the plan directs, keeping each stream separate.
Hold uncertain material and refer it. Do not add it to a general bin.
Record each bag or load, its stream, its destination and the handover.
Sign off a handover only where the route is authorised.

workedExamples.situation: A contractor suggests putting demolition debris into the office waste bins.
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse. Verify the authorised waste route, hold the debris for an authorised handover, and record the proposal and the refusal.

workedExamples.situation: Bagged mouldy paper is ready to go, but the same area had sewage-affected water.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the bags go in normal waste?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not until the stream is confirmed. The guideline's statement on bagged mouldy material is about mould itself, and it does not settle the stream for material that also came into contact with contaminated water. Hold the bags, record them and refer.

equipmentAndPpe: Waste-stream register with fields for stream, destination and handover.
Labelled holding area for uncertain material.
Training-only mock labels and worksheet. No real waste is moved in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Putting demolition debris into ordinary office bins.
commonErrors.prevention: Refuse. Verify the authorised route before any handling.

commonErrors.error: Assuming all mouldy material follows one waste stream.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the stream for each load, including any contaminated water or hazardous material.

commonErrors.error: Handing over waste without a record.
commonErrors.prevention: Record each bag or load, its destination and the handover.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Hazardous and regulated waste handling is restricted to competent and, where required, licensed people. This lesson does not grant authority to transport or dispose of it.
Local waste rules govern destinations. The rules in other states and territories were not checked for this lesson.

qualityStandard: The learner identifies the stream of each load in a described scene.
The learner refuses an unauthorised route.
The learner records each load, its stream, its destination and its handover.
documentationEvidence: Waste-stream register with the stream, destination and handover for each load.
Refusal or referral record for any unauthorised route.
summary: Confirm the authorised route before handling.
Do not add uncertain material to a general bin.

knowledgeChecks.question: A contractor suggests putting demolition debris into the office bins. What is correct?
options: Agree, because it is only a few bags.
Refuse, verify the authorised route and record the proposal.
Agree if the bins are in the back yard.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the WA guideline say about bagged mouldy material?
options: It must be burned on site.
Mould is not considered hazardous waste, and bagged mouldy material can go in normal waste.

knowledgeChecks.question: Bagged mouldy material is linked to a sewage-affected area. What should happen?
options: Hold the bags, record them and refer, because the stream is not confirmed.
Put it in normal waste, as the guideline says mould is not hazardous.
Empty the bags into the drain.

officialReferences.title: Guidelines for managing mould and dampness: related public health risks in buildings (WA Department of Health)
officialReferences.pageDate: April 2024 (version control table); publication code ENV-0014702 MAY'24; no separate last-updated date shown
officialReferences.covers: Read through a page-summary tool on 2026-11-03 (PDF, Environmental Health Directorate, WA Department of Health). Section 1.4 sets out a general public health duty, a workplace duty and a residential tenancies duty. Section 2.1 names people with existing respiratory, immunocompromising and allergic conditions, and infants, children and older people. Section 3.2.2 says porous items are often not economically salvageable and must be thrown out. Section 3.3 says the source must be located to address the cause and prevent recurrence. Section 3.4.1 defines simple contamination as new, isolated and visible, no greater than one square metre, with easily identified causes, and its footnote calls the one-square-metre size arbitrary. Section 3.4.2 defines complex contamination as larger than one square metre or found in multiple rooms or places. Section 3.5 states there are no defined quantitative or qualitative exposure thresholds for mould or dampness. Section 4.1 lists containment, drying and source repair as principles. Section 4.2.2 advises scrubbing hard surfaces with soapy water, avoiding dry brushing, cleaning at least 30 to 50 cm beyond the visible mould, removing or discarding porous items that cannot be adequately cleaned, stating that mould is not considered hazardous waste, and not painting, sealing or covering surfaces until dry. Section 4.3 recommends a site-specific plan with professionals for complex contamination, isolation with heavy grade plastic and negative pressure, and evacuation of occupants. Section 4.4 lists no recurrence within two to four weeks after remediation as an indicator of success, recommends the evaluation be done by a different entity, and states there are no legal requirements for a post-remediation assessment. Appendix B recommends a P2 or N95 respirator and says PAPRs should be used for complex remediation. Appendix E says mould can grow within 24 to 48 hours in flood-affected homes.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to remediate, demolish, disturb building materials, handle contaminated water or waste, or certify that a building, room or occupant area is safe or free of mould or pathogens. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Restricted or high-exposure remediation is carried out only by an appropriately qualified and competent professional under an approved plan, and some related work, including asbestos and lead disturbance and certain waste handling, is restricted to licensed or specially authorised people. The owner, manager, tenant or contract may define what work is permitted, but where the contract covers only routine cleaning, that is the limit of the task. Where the controlling authority or the competent supervisor is not identified, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: the hazards are unknown or changing; the work is destructive or hazardous and outside the authorised scope; exposure is uncontrolled or the building is unsafe to occupy; supervision, equipment or permissions are insufficient; flood, sewage, asbestos or lead may be present; a worker's PPE or respirator readiness has not been verified; a client asks for a clearance or pathogen-free statement; or a waste route is unauthorised. A stop-work decision is correct. Record it and restart only after the competent supervisor has confirmed the scope in writing.
